_about: General week-by-week notes for Bloomly. Information only, not medical advice. Written from public guidance by the NHS (nhs.uk/pregnancy/week-by-week), ACOG (acog.org) and Mayo Clinic (mayoclinic.org). Sizes are approximate: crown to rump up to week 19, head to heel from week 20.

4.body: The tiny embryo is settling into the lining of your womb.
4.tip: If you haven't already, a daily folic acid supplement is commonly recommended.
4.ask: When should I book my first pregnancy appointment?

5.body: The neural tube, which becomes the brain and spine, is forming.
5.tip: Tiredness is very common now. Rest whenever you can.
5.ask: Are my current medicines and supplements okay to keep taking?

6.body: A tiny heart has started to beat and small buds for arms and legs appear.
6.tip: Feeling sick? Small, frequent snacks and plain foods can help.
6.ask: When will my first scan be?

7.body: The face is starting to take shape and the brain is growing quickly.
7.tip: Ginger biscuits or ginger tea help some people with nausea.
7.ask: Which screening tests will I be offered?

8.body: Fingers and toes are beginning to form.
8.tip: Keep a water bottle nearby. Sipping often is easier than big glasses.
8.ask: Which foods should I avoid while pregnant?

9.body: The main organs are all forming and tiny muscles are developing.
9.tip: Comfortable, supportive clothing can make a real difference now.
9.ask: Is my usual exercise still okay?

10.body: Baby can make small movements, although you won't feel them yet.
10.tip: Many people find a short walk lifts energy and mood.
10.ask: What does my booking appointment include?

11.body: Baby's head is large compared with the body, and nails are starting to grow.
11.tip: Gentle stretching before bed may help you sleep.
11.ask: When is the dating scan, and what will it show?

12.body: The placenta is taking on more of the work of supporting baby.
12.tip: Nausea often starts to ease around now for many people.
12.ask: Can we talk through the results of my early screening?

13.body: Tiny fingerprints are forming on baby's fingertips.
13.tip: You are nearly into the second trimester. Be kind to yourself.
13.ask: How much weight gain is typical for me?

14.body: Baby can make small facial expressions, like squinting.
14.tip: Many people find their energy returns in the second trimester.
14.ask: When might I start to feel baby move?

15.body: Baby's bones are getting harder and the skin is very thin.
15.tip: Pregnancy yoga or swimming can be gentle ways to stay active.

16.body: Baby's back muscles are getting stronger and the head is held more upright.
16.tip: Sleeping on your side with a pillow between your knees can feel more comfortable.
16.ask: Should I have any vaccines during pregnancy?

17.body: A layer of fat is starting to form under baby's skin.
17.tip: Iron-rich foods like beans, lentils and leafy greens are a good addition.
17.ask: Do I need to have my iron levels checked?

18.body: Baby can probably hear muffled sounds, including your voice.
18.tip: Talking or singing to your bump is a lovely way to connect.
18.ask: What does the mid-pregnancy scan check for?

19.body: A protective waxy coating called vernix is covering baby's skin.
19.tip: Heartburn? Smaller meals and staying upright after eating can help.
19.ask: Which sleeping position do you recommend for me?

20.body: Halfway there! Many people start to feel little flutters around now.
20.tip: Take a moment to celebrate getting halfway.
20.ask: Can we start talking about my birth preferences?

21.body: Baby is swallowing small amounts of fluid, which helps the gut develop.
21.tip: Night-time leg cramps are common. Calf stretches may help.
21.ask: What antenatal classes are available near me?

22.body: Baby's grip is getting stronger and the eyes are formed.
22.tip: Comfortable, supportive shoes can ease foot and back aches.
22.ask: What changes in movement should I look out for?

23.body: Baby's lungs are developing, ready for breathing later on.
23.tip: Pelvic floor exercises are worth starting if you haven't already.
23.ask: Will I be offered a test for gestational diabetes?

24.body: Baby is growing steadily and the face is fully formed.
24.tip: Getting to know baby's usual pattern of movements is a good habit.
24.ask: When will I be offered the whooping cough vaccine?

25.body: Baby's hands are active, exploring their face and the cord.
25.tip: Stay active in ways that feel good for you.
25.ask: Which warning signs mean I should call you straight away?

26.body: Baby's eyes can open and close, and they may respond to light.
26.tip: Antenatal classes can be a good place to meet other parents-to-be.
26.ask: Can we talk about skin-to-skin and feeding after birth?

27.body: Baby's brain is very busy and you might notice hiccups.
27.tip: Go to sleep on your side in the third trimester. It's the current advice.
27.ask: What happens if labour starts early?

28.body: Welcome to the third trimester. Baby can blink and is gaining weight.
28.tip: Learn baby's usual movement pattern. If it slows or changes, contact your midwife or doctor straight away.
28.ask: How often will my appointments be from now on?

29.body: Baby is laying down more fat and growing stronger.
29.tip: You might like to start thinking about what to pack for the birth.
29.ask: Where would you recommend I give birth?

30.body: Baby's brain and nervous system are developing quickly.
30.tip: Accept offers of help. Rest is productive too.
30.ask: When should I write down my birth preferences?

31.body: Baby can turn their head from side to side.
31.tip: Movements may feel different as space gets tighter, but they shouldn't reduce.
31.ask: What feeding support is available after birth?

32.body: Many babies are now settling head-down, though some turn later.
32.tip: Short naps or putting your feet up can help with swelling.
32.ask: What position is baby lying in?

33.body: Baby's immune system is getting a boost from you.
33.tip: Breathing and relaxation exercises are good to practise now.
33.ask: What are my options if I go past my due date?

34.body: Baby's lungs and nervous system keep maturing.
34.tip: Swollen feet are common. Rest with them raised when you can.
34.ask: What pain relief options are there in labour?

35.body: Baby is putting on weight quickly now.
35.tip: If you'll travel by car with baby, check the car seat fits.
35.ask: What happens at my next appointment?

36.body: Baby's skull bones stay soft so they can move through the birth canal.
36.tip: Prepare a few easy meals for the early days after birth.
36.ask: How will I know when labour is starting?

37.body: Baby is now considered early term and keeps practising breathing.
37.tip: Keep your maternity notes and bag somewhere easy to grab.
37.ask: When should I call you or come in?

38.body: Baby's organs are ready for life outside the womb.
38.tip: Rest, eat well and keep sipping water.
38.ask: What happens if my waters break?

39.body: Baby is fully grown and getting ready to meet you.
39.tip: Gentle walks and plenty of rest. Listen to your body.
39.ask: What happens if I go past 40 weeks?

40.body: Your due date week. Only a small number of babies arrive exactly on it.
40.tip: You've come so far. Be gentle with yourself.
40.ask: What monitoring will I have if baby is late?
